key_insight: METTA proposes memory-enhanced test-time adaptation to help reinforcement learning agents adapt quickly to unfamiliar tasks. It targets a key trade-off: retaining useful evidence from long interaction histories without the quadratic costs of transformer-based retrieval.
problem_solved: Meta-reinforcement learning agents must learn about new tasks from limited interaction while remembering earlier evidence. Recurrent agents compress that evidence into hidden states, while transformer-based approaches face quadratic memory and computation costs.
method: Introduce Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation (METTA) for meta-reinforcement learning.
Use a memory-enhanced approach to support adaptation from interaction history at test time.
Decompose the fast adaptation phase; the supplied abstract is truncated before the components and implementation are explained.
impact: The approach targets more practical adaptation for agents that need to use long histories under resource constraints. The provided excerpt does not include results, so performance and efficiency gains cannot be confirmed.
visual_elements: Trade-off diagram: recurrent hidden-state compression versus transformer history retrieval.
Conceptual loop: interact with a new task → retain task evidence → adapt → act.

Memory and compute icons illustrating the resource challenge of long histories.
paper_title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
